    LOCAL TEXTS · SHARED TOKEN IDENTITIES · PATTERN POPULATIONS

    One sequence, one pattern node.

    The illustration associates each token position with one binary matching input. With N positions and a wildcard allowance of K, at least N − K positions must match.

    The dim contacts show one possible wildcard mask. The allowance covers every permitted mask, not just the positions shown. A wildcard permits a mismatch or inactive input; it does not require one.

    This is a visual analogy for the pattern model. A stored sequence includes the proposed next token; the prediction workspace will distinguish that output from the preceding inputs.

    Configuration and Train share a text queue. Training decomposes full windows into exact and wildcard patterns in three sorted packed tiers. Generation uses exact prefix matches, shorter suffixes, and learned token frequencies. Context steering will be defined later. The earlier prototype remains available in Train.
